# Empty state

What a collection shows when it has nothing in it: why it is empty, and the one thing to do about it.

**Not implemented yet.** This page is the *approved intent* — the props API signed off at gate 1 of the build order, before any React exists. Do not import it; there is nothing to import.

| | |
|---|---|
| Registry name | `empty-state` |
| Family | feedback |
| Tier | free |
| Status (css / react / figma) | future / future / future |
| Depends on | `icon` |

## Behavior

A `div` with a title, an optional description and an optional action, rendered where the empty collection would be. Silent by default; `live` announces it when it appears because of something the reader did, as Notice's `live` does. No primitive: no interaction to own and no state to hold.

- **Empty is not an error** — "No invoices yet" and "Couldn't load invoices" look alike and mean opposite things — one is a correct answer, the other is a failure the reader may need to retry or report. A failure is a Notice with the danger variant, in the same place. Keeping them apart stops a failed request from quietly telling the reader they have no data.
- **Two kinds of empty, and the copy differs, not the component** — First use — nothing has been created yet — wants an invitation and the action that creates the first item. No results — a search or filter matched nothing — wants the query restated and a way to clear it. Both are the same layout with different words; a `kind` prop would be a switch that changes nothing visible. The usage cases below are where the difference is written down.
- **The title is a styled paragraph, not a heading** — The empty state sits inside a section that already has a heading — the list's own — and cannot know its level, which is the problem Notice solves the same way. A heading here would add an outline entry for content that does not exist. The section's own heading, still visible above it, is what names the area.
- **`live` is a prop, silent by default** — Notice's reasoning, applied unchanged. An empty state present when the page loads is read in place, and announcing it would interrupt the page being read. One that appears because the reader typed a search that matched nothing must be announced, because their attention is on the search field and the list changed somewhere else. That depends on how the empty state arrived, not on what it says, so the caller states it.
- **One action, at most** — An empty state exists to get the reader out of it. One action — Create the first one, Clear filters — is the way out; two is a choice the reader did not come here to make. Secondary help belongs in the description as a link.
- **An icon, never an illustration** — Illustrations are brand, they carry no token, and they push the action below the fold on a phone. A `size.icon.lg` glyph in `theme.fg.muted` marks the area as intentionally empty without competing with the text. It is `aria-hidden`: the title says what it means.
- **Line length: size.measure.compact** — The description is bounded at size.measure.compact, 45ch — short enough to read as one thought, centred under its heading, and in ch so it follows the text. Settled by the token interview (docs/decisions/2026-11-gate-1-review.md).
- **Web and native** — Web: a `div`; with `live`, it carries `role="status"` (polite) or `role="alert"` (assertive), as Notice does. The icon is `aria-hidden`. React Native: a `View`; the title is plain `Text`, not `accessibilityRole="header"`, for the outline reason above. `live` maps to `accessibilityLiveRegion` on Android and to `AccessibilityInfo.announceForAccessibility` with the title on iOS. All props work on both. Rata-drawn (decision N5): React Native exposes no OS empty-state view, so it is drawn from the same recipe as the web. The native implementation ships in the pro tier (decision N6).

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | `string` | — | What is empty, said plainly. |
| `description?` | `ReactNode` | — | One or two sentences on why it is empty or what the action will do. |
| `action?` | `ReactNode` | — | The one way out: a Button or a Link. |
| `icon?` | `LucideIcon \| false` | — | A glyph marking the area as intentionally empty. Omit for none. |
| `live?` | `"off" \| "polite" \| "assertive"` | `"off"` | Whether the empty state is announced when it appears. |
| `className?` | `string` | — | Extra classes, for placement. |

### `title`

```ts
title: string
```

What is empty, said plainly.

**Use when**

- First use: "No invoices yet".
- No results: "No tokens match ‘brand-teal’" — restate the query, so the reader can see what they typed.

**Don't use for**

- "Nothing here" or "Oops". Say what is missing.
- Reporting a failure. "Couldn't load" is a Notice.

**Accessibility** Read first, and announced on its own when `live` is set.

### `description`

```ts
description?: ReactNode
```

One or two sentences on why it is empty or what the action will do.

**Use when**

- What the first item will be for, or which filter is excluding everything.

**Don't use for**

- Repeating the title in more words.

### `action`

```ts
action?: ReactNode
```

The one way out: a Button or a Link.

**Use when**

- Create the first item; clear the search or filters.

**Don't use for**

- Two buttons. Put secondary help in the description as a link.

**Accessibility** A real control, reached by Tab in reading order after the text.

### `icon`

```ts
icon?: LucideIcon | false
```

A glyph marking the area as intentionally empty. Omit for none.

**Use when**

- An icon for the kind of thing that is missing — a file for documents, a search glyph for no results.

**Don't use for**

- An illustration or image. This slot is an icon at the icon scale's largest step.

**Accessibility** Always `aria-hidden`; the title carries the meaning.

### `live`

```ts
live?: "off" | "polite" | "assertive" = "off"
```

Whether the empty state is announced when it appears.

**Use when**

- `polite` for no-results after a search or filter the reader just changed.

**Don't use for**

- `polite` on an empty state present at page load. It interrupts the page being read.
- `assertive`, almost ever. Being empty is not urgent.

**Accessibility** The same contract as Notice's `live`: a live region announces changes, so this matters only when the empty state arrives after the page did.

### `className`

```ts
className?: string
```

Extra classes, for placement.

**Use when**

- Positioning it in the space the content would fill.

**Don't use for**

- Boxing it in a card. It replaces content; it is not a widget.

## Use cases

### First use

A collection the reader has not created anything in yet.

```tsx
<EmptyState
  icon={FileText}
  title="No invoices yet"
  description="Invoices you send will appear here, newest first."
  action={<Button>Create invoice</Button>}
/>
```

Silent, because it is there when the page loads. One action, the one that ends the empty state.

### No results after a search

A filter or search the reader just changed matched nothing.

```tsx
<EmptyState
  live="polite"
  icon={SearchX}
  title={`No tokens match ‘${query}’`}
  action={<Button variant="secondary" onClick={clearSearch}>Clear search</Button>}
/>
```

`live="polite"` because the reader's focus is in the search field and the list changed somewhere else. The title restates the query, so a typo is visible.

### Reaching for the wrong component

The request for the list failed.

```tsx
<EmptyState title="No invoices" />
```

Don't. Telling the reader they have no invoices when the request failed is the worst message on the page. That is a Notice with `variant="danger"` and a retry action.

## Token recipe

### base

Centred text in the space the content would have filled, with no box: an empty state replaces content, so it sits on the content's surface rather than on a card of its own.

| Property | Token |
|---|---|
| padding-block | `space.padding.lg` |
| text-align | `center` |
| max-inline-size | `size.measure.compact` |
| icon size | `size.icon.lg` |
| icon color | `theme.fg.muted` |
| gap between icon and title | `space.stack.sm` |
| title font-size | `type.large.size` |
| title font-weight | `type.heading.weight` |
| title line-height | `type.large.line-height` |
| title color | `theme.fg.primary` |
| gap between title and description | `space.stack.2xs` |
| description font-size | `type.body.size` |
| description color | `theme.fg.secondary` |
| gap above the action | `space.stack.md` |
